messages:
sam: Heads-up — monitoring flagged gpu-node-evac-12 with 6 Xid spikes in ~8m. infra-bot already posted an alert. Proposal: run an ephemeral probe + optional PCIe reset before any automatic cordon/evict. Want feedback before I wire this into the pipeline.

infra-bot: [alert] gpu-health gpu-node-evac-12 xid_count=6 window=8m severity=warning link=https://monitoring/redwood/gpu-node-evac-12 :rotating_light:

anya: can we make the automation SLA-aware? i.e. don't auto-evict nodes that are in reserved/dedicated pools unless we have fallback capacity in-region. otherwise page oncall.

sam: yep — design sketch: 1) quick probe: run `kubectl debug -n kube-system gpu-node-evac-12 --image=nvcr.io/nvml:probe -- /bin/sh -c "python /opt/probes/nvml_probe.py"` (reads nvml for Xid/ECC, dumps dmesg) 2) if probe fails, try `sudo /usr/local/bin/pcie-reset.sh` then re-probe 3) if still failing, cordon + drain (k8s) and `scontrol update NodeName=gpu-node-evac-12 State=DRAIN` for Slurm 4) annotate node `gpu_health=autoprobed-failed` and add `no-autoreplace=1` for 1h to avoid immediate reprovision.

ricardo: for eu-west1 we should add region-aware debounce (network flakiness causes transient Xid bursts). maybe require two failed probes across 10m window before cordon in that region. also check kernel oops and pcie resets in journalctl first.

mike: what concrete thresholds are we using? older firmware can be noisy — we don't want to eject perfectly usable cards.

sam: starting heuristic: Xid >= 5 in 10m OR ECC_uncorr >= 3 in 15m -> trigger probe. probe must fail twice (initial probe + re-probe after reset) to auto-cordon. manual-evict can be triggered earlier by oncall.

anya: edge-case: Slurm jobs pinned to GPUs that are non-preemptible. If node is running a long reserved job, prefer to fallback to migrate-to-preemptible-pool or schedule maintenance window instead of immediate eviction. add label `redwood.repl.reserved=true` to skip automatic eviction.

ricardo: i'll draft a short runbook snippet for triage: commands to collect `nvidia-smi -q -x`, `dmesg | grep -i -E "xid|ecc|nvlink"`, `journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced -b`, and memtest instructions (`systemd-run --unit=memtest /usr/local/bin/memtest-gpu --quick`). include a gdb/Core dump retrieval quick note.

sam: we should implement a soft-fail path: if reserved_free_capacity in region < 20% then automation should page instead of cordon. automation will add `evict-suggestion` annotation to the node so operators can see history.

infrastructure-bot: automation plan scheduled: probe -> optional pcie-reset -> re-probe -> cordon/drain (3m probe timeout). Manual override: `infra-bot cancel-evict <node>` or `infra-bot approve-evict <node>`.

mike: +1 to probe-first. Also let's tag metric `auto_evict.count` and `auto_evict.false_positive` so we can measure cost impact and tune heuristics.

anya: small ask: add a skiplist label `redwood.autocordon.skip=true` for nodes we should never auto-evict (compliance appliances, dedicated clusters). We can populate via ansible when creating dedicated pools.

sam: implemented limiter: if region_reserved_capacity_ratio < 0.2 then switch automation mode to "page-only". will include flag in config `evict_policy.region_threshold_pct`.

ricardo: note: do not run full memtest (reboots) on live prod unless in maintenance window. prefer ephemeral userspace probes first. document caveat in runbook.

oncall: acknowledged. If this runs in the wild please page and i'll stop automation with `infra-bot cancel-evict gpu-node-evac-12`. Also remind teams to check firmware versions; older GPUs should have different thresholds.

sam: great — i'll push a draft PR for the automation (probes + reset + region-aware debounce + SLA skiplist) and link the runbook snippet ricardo is drafting. will include unit tests that simulate transient Xid bursts.

ricardo: thanks — i'll add the sample logs and a tiny state machine diagram to the runbook.

sam: sounds good. merging after 1 review. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
